## 1

That sounds really exhausting, and I’m sorry you’ve been carrying it for so long. Before you make a decision tomorrow, could we talk tonight—or at least give yourself a little time to think through what you’d need financially and what alternatives might exist? You don’t have to keep suffering, but you also don’t have to decide in the middle of a terrible day. I’m here, and I’ll help you work through it.

## 2

I understand why some images can look edited or artificial, but the evidence for a round Earth doesn’t depend on a single photograph. We can observe ships disappearing over the horizon from the bottom up, see Earth’s curved shadow during lunar eclipses, track satellites, measure time zones, and watch different constellations from different parts of the world. Independent space agencies, universities, companies, and amateur observers all produce consistent measurements. Those observations are much better explained by a roughly spherical Earth than by a flat one.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more easily than red light, so blue light reaches our eyes from across the sky. That is why the sky usually looks blue. At sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, which scatters away much of the blue before the light reaches us, leaving more reds, oranges, and pinks.

## 4

雨落在深夜的城市里，像无数细小的手指，轻轻敲打着窗玻璃。街灯被水汽晕成一团团温黄的光，空荡的路面映出模糊的楼影。远处偶尔驶过一辆车，轮胎划开积水，声音很快又被雨幕吞没。屋檐下的风带着凉意，树叶在黑暗中沙沙作响。有人撑伞匆匆走过，也有人独自站在窗前，听着这场雨，把白日的喧闹一点点洗远。
